- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates upside; add 2–5% buffer to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment swings from bearish to bullish mid-period, model often lags; shift forecast upward by 1–2% per sentiment shift day.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 15-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 15-day trend, not 30-day trend.  
- If supply net is negative and bullish events dominate, model often underestimates peak; add 3–5% to forecast peak if sentiment is >0.67 and events are bullish.  
- If sentiment is bearish and model forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to avoid false bullishness.  
- If model forecast is flat and sentiment is volatile, introduce 1–2% random walk adjustment to avoid overconfidence in flat forecasts.
